direction: Refine the L2a static merge score for the tight-capacity / clustered-eccentric-depot weak regimes: keep global depot-scale normalization mean(d[0,1:]) as the single dimensional denominator, and evolve (lambda in 1.00-1.20, radial asymmetry mu in 0.08-0.20, dimensionless fill reward beta in 0.05-0.20) plus a symmetric endpoint-demand-balance term so that route-end merges pack loads closer to Q without destroying large-savings edges; keep the single vectorized pre-pass scoring (no per-merge rescoring) to preserve the ~2 ms budget margin at 25 ms.

operations.mechanism: KB entry method-cvrp-m2-l2a-generalized-savings establishes that (a) the global depot-distance scale is the mandatory denominator (per-pair normalization degrades dev_24 from ~16.22 to ~18.0), (b) generalized savings with lam 1.00-1.15, mu 0.08-0.15 and a beta 0.05-0.15 fill term reaches 16.1398 on dev_24 with zero postprocess and p95 ~2.4 ms at n up to 200 — well inside the 25 ms budget, and (c) the combination of an evolved merge seed with relocate_2opt was left as an explicitly unverified item. Our archive already holds a stronger evolved variant at 16.1086 with intra_2opt, and the residual portfolio gap over VBS is only 0.37% concentrated in tight-capacity clustered/eccentric instances, so the highest-value remaining lever is the dimensionless fill/endpoint-balance reward (targeting tight-capacity fragmentation) rather than a more expensive dynamic interface, which KB method-cvrp-m2-l2b-dynamic-state-merge showed triggers budget-exhaustion degradation at 25 ms. intra_2opt keeps the O(1)-delta local polish that KB method-cvrp-intra-2opt validates, applied per route after the deterministic merge.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Because the weakest regimes are capacity_level=tight (12/24 instances) and spatial=clustered/eccentric depot, adding a dimensionless capacity-fill reward beta*clip((q_i+q_j)/Q,0,1) with an endpoint imbalance term (1-|q_i-q_j|/(q_i+q_j)) and mild lambda>1 edge dampening inside the globally depot-scale-normalized static score will reduce terminal fragment routes under tight capacity and lower mean tour length on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 below the current SBS 16.1086, while remaining deterministic, scale-invariant, and fully convergent within the 25 ms budget.
